---
title: "Storefront on Start + Void"
description: "Native Storefront Worker, the cutover artifact, and the cutover and Vercel rollback packet."
updatedAt: "2026-11-09"
audience: developers
---

Storefront (`apps/storefront`) runs on TanStack Start, Vite+ and Void behind
[`@tuturuuu/start-bridge`](/build/devops/start-bridge) with the React Server
Components plugin. The Next.js build (`build`) and the Vercel project stay in
place until the cutover has been stable, so the canonical host keeps a one-step
route back.

## Worker profiles

| Profile | Worker | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source default (`void.config.ts`) | `tuturuuu-storefront-vite-staging` | `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1`, no routes, `workers_dev` and `preview_urls` off |
| Cutover artifact | `tuturuuu-storefront` | `storefront-cloudflare.yaml` rewrites the emitted Wrangler config: `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=0`, `TUTURUUU_REQUIRE_SECRETS=1`, `preview_urls=false`, source maps off |

The Worker declares no routes. The hostname is attached at cutover by the
release operator. With `TUTURUUU_REQUIRE_SECRETS=1` the Worker answers `503
Service misconfigured` (no-store) until `INVENTORY_APP_URL`,
`SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` and `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET` are present
(`cloudflare/startup.ts`). Names only are recorded here.

## Request ownership

| Request | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `store.tuturuuu.com`, `storefront.tutur3u.com` | Canonical hosts. |
| `storefront.tuturuuu.com`, `stores.tuturuuu.com`, `storefronts.tuturuuu.com` | `307` to `https://store.tuturuuu.com` with path and query preserved. |
| `/` | Redirects to `/demo`. |
| `/api/build-info` | Local build identity. |
| `/api/v1/inventory/*` | Forwarded to `INVENTORY_APP_URL`. |
| Other `/api/*` | Forwarded to `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN` (default `https://tuturuuu.com`). |
| Unknown host | Rejected. |

Every response carries `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` from the app's
response wrapper.

## Build and artifact

`storefront-cloudflare.yaml` builds the Worker, rejects route-tree drift,
records the emitted configuration receipt, runs the emitted-Worker runtime
suites (`cloudflare/*.runtime.mjs`) and uploads `storefront-cutover-production-<source SHA>`
(14 days). It never deploys. Do not run `build:cloudflare` on a shared
development machine.

## Cutover packet

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Worker | `tuturuuu-storefront` |
| Route | `store.tuturuuu.com/*`, plus the redirect aliases above; operator-attached |
| Static assets binding | `ASSETS` (`dist/client`, `run_worker_first`) |
| Build command | `bun run --cwd apps/storefront build:cloudflare` (the workflow then applies the production overrides) |
| Secrets (names) | `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET` |
| Vars | `INVENTORY_APP_URL=https://inventory.tuturuuu.com`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://store.tuturuuu.com`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_APP_URL=https://tuturuuu.com` |
| Prior Vercel deployment | record the immutable deployment ID and URL of the `storefront` Vercel project before the switch |
| Data | no database writes and no migrations |

### Switch

1. Record the source SHA, the artifact name and the Vercel deployment ID.
2. Provision the secrets on `tuturuuu-storefront`, deploy the artifact, and
   run the smoke below against the Worker's own address.
3. Attach `store.tuturuuu.com` (a proxied route in front of the still-valid
   Vercel origin where possible), then the alias hosts.

### Smoke

```bash
# Entry route and no 5xx
curl -sI https://store.tuturuuu.com/ | head -5
# Login page renders
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://store.tuturuuu.com/login
# Build identity matches the accepted SHA
curl -s https://store.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info
# Alias host redirects to the canonical host
curl -sI https://storefront.tuturuuu.com/ | head -3
```

Expected: a redirect to `/demo`, `200`, the accepted commit, and a `307` to
`store.tuturuuu.com`.

### Rollback

- **Triggers:** 5xx above 1% for 5 minutes, a wrong redirect, a checkout
  handoff failure, or a private store served anonymously.
- **Action:** remove the Worker route (or repoint the mapping) so the hosts
  resolve to the recorded Vercel deployment. Never rebuild on the rollback path.
- **Data:** a route rollback changes no catalog, order or payment data.
- **Stability:** keep the Vercel project and domains for 14 consecutive stable
  days before decommissioning, which is a separate approval.
